title: What do the orange and blue grids give in the game?
description: The circle and strike game is played on an orange grid and a blue grid. Each grid is played once and again with other circles, and each keeps its own total.
teaching_notes: One idea: the game gives a fixed total for each grid, and different grids have different totals. Watch for students who expect two grids to share one answer because the game is the same.

video_script.why: The child plays the circle and strike game on two new grids and finds the total of each.
video_script.substitution: The book's own orange grid and blue grid.
video_script.anchor: an orange grid and a blue grid of plus and minus numbers from the book
video_script.payoff_line: Each grid keeps its own total, negative eight for orange and negative fourteen for blue.

final_answer.spoken: the orange grid gives negative eight, and the blue grid gives negative fourteen

maths_rules: orange grid (grid 1) as given: row 1 is 7, 10, 13, 16; row 2 is -2, 1, 4, 7; row 3 is -11, -8, -5, -2; row 4 is -20, -7, -14, -11
check, orange: 16, -2, -8, -14 make -8; check, blue: -8, -7, -2, 3 make -14
circle one number in each row and each column; a plus number moves up and a minus number moves down
video_script.design: The orange grid and the blue grid side by side. Each play is circled and added one at a time on an upright number line, teal for moving up and amber for moving down. A second play is shown on each grid as the check.
open_questions: The orange grid's row 4, column 2 is printed as -7 in the source text, though the pattern of the other numbers suggests -17. No play in this video circles that tile, so the totals hold either way.
